frontier.hypothesis: Cluster B (4 diffs) is closable by giving the three early exits a constant-1 return, provided jump2 can be made to keep the MID-function copy of the shared `li v0,1 / j` block instead of relocating it to the function end.
frontier.mechanism: jump.c find_cross_jump decides which of two identical tails survives and redirects the other; when the surviving copy is the late one the rejection chain's last `beq` inverts to a `bne` and one instruction is added. Downstream, reorg.c fill_simple_delay_slots can only leave `li v0,1` in the `j`'s slot when the block carries a label with real predecessors.
frontier.next_probe: Dump .jump2 for tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s6/v5.c (pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_800283D0 with that body in place) and read which block find_cross_jump keeps and which is redirected, then look for a source arrangement in which the chain-fallthrough copy is the survivor. This is the same jump_chain-ordering question as diamond 2, so one instrumented read may settle both clusters at once.

frontier.hypothesis: The s2/s3 rotation (12 diffs) flips if arg1's home pseudo 73 has live_length in [38,65] instead of 92 - the second solution branch of the allocno window, never tried.
frontier.mechanism: global.c:635-655 allocno_compare with flow.c-computed reg_live_length; target's callee-saved map is exactly the sorted order 72,77,73,143,75,90,79, satisfied whenever 2142 < 140000/L73 < 3698. Unlike the L143 branch this requires liveness to be REMOVED, so the 215==215 instruction budget does not foreclose it.
frontier.next_probe: Reverse the s5 liveness dial (tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s5/dial.sh): measure how many insns each region of arg1's live range contributes to L73 by probing at each of the six func_80032854 call sites and reading the ALLOCDBG livelen for pseudo 73, then look for a region where arg1 could honestly be dead in the original's shape (for example if the original re-derived the third argument rather than holding the parameter live across the whole body).

frontier.hypothesis: The tail a0/a1 quantity cluster (7 diffs, cluster E) is a local-alloc quantity-order decision whose window has never been measured - the only cluster on the function with an entirely unvalidated model.
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc.c qty_compare_1: pri = floor_log2(n_refs)*n_refs*size/(death-birth)*10000, ties broken by ascending quantity number. Hand-derived at s3 as pri(qty0 pointer)=4000 vs pri(qty3 Judge[] element)=5000, so a tie suffices; requirement is span(qty0) <= 24 (from 30) or span(qty3) >= 6 (from 4).
frontier.next_probe: Build the local-alloc analogue of s5/dial.sh using BB2_QTY_DEBUG=1 (harness at tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s3/qty.sh), dial 2-insn filler between the `lh Judge($at)` and the `mult` and separately inside qty0's span, and record the measured flip window in both directions BEFORE proposing any C. qty0 is a COMBINED quantity (sll producer + temp_a0 + var_a1), so the co-moving denominators must be read from the trace, not assumed - the s5 experience is that a hand-derived window can be wrong by a factor of two.
